report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/adapters/transport.py chunk 1/1: 4 symbols (TransportSink, InMemoryTransportSink, JsonlTransportSink, CompositeTransportSink) with claims about persistence, fan-out, and append-only behavior. Some claims uncheckable due to dependency on TransportRecord.
risks: JsonlTransportSink.publish | medium | Uses record.to_dict() which is not defined in this chunk; if missing or returns non-serializable, will raise AttributeError or TypeError. | Check TransportRecord.to_dict() method existence and return type.

JsonlTransportSink.publish | low | Uses json.dumps with default=str, which may silently convert non-serializable objects to their string representation, potentially losing data fidelity. | Verify that all fields in TransportRecord are natively JSON-serializable.

InMemoryTransportSink | low | No concurrency protection; if publish is called from multiple tasks, appends may interleave but list append is thread-safe in CPython, though not atomic in general. | Assess whether asyncio concurrency is expected; if so, consider adding a lock.

handoff.purpose: Define transport sink protocol and three implementations: in-memory, JSONL file, and composite fan-out.

symbols.name: TransportSink
symbols.note: Async protocol requiring publish method accepting TransportRecord.

symbols.name: InMemoryTransportSink
symbols.note: Collects records in a list for testing.

symbols.name: JsonlTransportSink
symbols.note: Appends JSON lines to a file, with directory creation and async lock.

symbols.name: CompositeTransportSink
symbols.note: Iterates over sinks and publishes to each sequentially.

claims.text: Small deterministic sink for tests and embedded consumers.
claims.why: The sink stores records in a list, which is deterministic and suitable for tests.

claims.text: Append-only JSONL journal preserving every normalized input/output.
claims.why: The code appends to a file with 'a' mode, but 'preserving every normalized input/output' depends on TransportRecord.to_dict() and the calling context, which are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Fan one record out to multiple sinks; failures remain visible.
claims.why: The publish method iterates over sinks and awaits each, so if a sink raises, the exception propagates immediately, making failures visible.

observations.what: JsonlTransportSink uses record.to_dict() which is not defined in this file; its existence and correctness cannot be verified.
InMemoryTransportSink has no concurrency protection; list append is not atomic across asyncio tasks.
JsonlTransportSink uses asyncio.Lock, but file I/O is blocking; this may block the event loop if the filesystem is slow.
